sect1.title: Plugin class
sect1.para: Plugin is a class, that handles shared data and triggered events to perform an I/O operations. It is dynamically linked to the user program by PDI. Behavior of each plugin is defined by specification tree in plugins subtree.
plugins: example: ... The given example will load example plugin and pass its subtree to the plugin's constructor.
The plugin has to inherit from PDI::Plugin and have a constructor with arguments PDI::Context& and PC_tree_t.

sect2.title: Adding a callback
sect2.para: PDI::Context has a member with all the functions (callbacks) that are called when user is sharing the data (calls PDI_share). To add a new function to the plugin must call callbacks().add_data_callback.

The first argument is the function to be called when user shares the data. If the second parameter (name) is given, the function will be called only on a specified data name. Returns a function that removes the callback from PDI::Context container.

sect1.title: Creating a true plugin: POSIX plugin

sect2.title: Step 1: Think what your plugin will be for.
sect2.para: Simple checkpointing. Each data will be saved in separate file. User can check the status of all files at once and then recover the data.

sect2.title: Step 2: Prepare your specification tree schema.
sect2.para:
data: some_data:{type:array,subtype:int,size:64} can_recover_data:int
plugins: posix: data: some_data:/file_path/ can_recover_all:can_recover_data /file_path/ is a path where to save and load from some_data. can_recover_data is a flag that indicates if the recover is possible.
The fastest way to learn is by examples. To show how to create a plugin, we will create "posix plugin". It won't do anything special, but give you a basic knowledge how to create one.

sect2.title: Step 3: Write your plugin.
